BiblicalUsage: Ayeph is weariness that goes to the bone — faint, languid, spent. Esau came from the field faint and sold his birthright for pottage, Gideon and his three hundred were faint yet pursuing, Isaiah promises that none shall be weary in the Lord's army, and God says he will satiate the weary soul and replenish every sorrowful soul.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Esau's bargain is the warning and Jeremiah's promise is the comfort. Weariness makes fools of us when we feed it with the wrong food, but God himself satisfies the weary soul.
